title: RAGE-toolkit/Artic-nf
description: Raw data processing and consensus generation

input.title: Input Options
input.description: Parameters for finding and handling input data for analysis.

rawfile_type.title: Raw file type
rawfile_type.description: Choose the raw file type from a given list.
rawfile_type.help_text: Available file types are fastq and fast5_pod5.

primer_schema.title: Primer schema
primer_schema.description: Path to a primer schema file.

basecaller.title: Basecaller to run
basecaller.description: Choose the basecaller from the given list.
basecaller.help_text: Available basecallers are Dorado and Guppy.

basecaller_program_dir.title: Basecaller program directory
basecaller_program_dir.description: Path to the basecaller program installation directory.

kit_name.title: Kit name
kit_name.help_text: You can get the barcode list from the Guppy or Dorado GitHub repositories.

sample_sheet.title: Sample sheet
sample_sheet.description: Workflow accepts the CSV file format.
sample_sheet.help_text: Refer to the GitHub repo for the correct sample sheet format.

prefix.title: Output filename prefix
prefix.description: Optional prefix attached to each of the output filenames.

advanced_options.title: Advanced Options
advanced_options.help_text: By default, these do not need to be changed unless you require tuning.

processed_fa_files.title: Processed FASTA files directory
processed_fa_files.description: Directory to store guppyplexed FASTQ files for Medaka.
processed_fa_files.help_text: This directory will be autogenerated by the workflow.

weeSAM_path.title: weeSAM path
weeSAM_path.description: Path to the weeSAM program for calculating stats.
weeSAM_path.help_text: This program must be cloned from its GitHub repository.

basecaller_config.title: Config file for basecaller
basecaller_config.help_text: Overrides default options. Allows for more customized basecalling/alignment.

threads.title: CPU threads
threads.description: Number of CPU threads to use for alignment.
threads.help_text: Minimap2 memory usage scales with thread count. Total resources are constrained by executor configuration.

resources.run_time: 1 minute per sample (depending on number of reads, length of reference, and available compute).
